transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes

Attendees:
- Alex Chen (Redwood, AE)
- Priya Ramesh (Redwood, SE)
- Marcus Lee (Zenith Analytics, Head of ML)
- Rosa Martinez (Zenith Analytics, Engineering Lead)
- Samir Khan (Zenith Analytics, CTO)

Summary: quick catalog walkthrough to converge on 2-3 open model candidates for a short pilot, review benchmark approach and runtime compatibility (GPU vs quantized CPU), and discuss enterprise constraints (VPC, SOC2, KMS).

Topics covered:
- catalog filtering and shortlist criteria (latency budget, cost, output quality)
- benchmark methodology and sample prompts
- runtime fit: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- compatibility matrix (kernel mapping, quantization support, sequence length limitations)
- security/compliance checklist and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm alex from redwood, joined by priya on the se side.
[00:08] Marcus Lee: morning, i'm marcus, head of ml at zenith. so we wanna move fast but need to validate latency and cost.
[00:14] Rosa Martinez: rosa here, i'll be owner of integration. we have strict VPC rules and SOC two requirements.
[00:20] Samir Khan: samir, cto. main ask is: can you meet a p95 under 800ms for our customer-facing summarization endpoint? and we need encryption at rest, KMS key control.
[00:32] Priya Ramesh: great, thanks. quick agenda: catalog shortlist, bench plan, runtime compatibility matrix, and security items. we'll demo the console filters then show a bench example.
[00:42] Alex Chen: i'll start with the catalog — we usually filter by model family, size, and verified throughput. for open models we recommend starting with 3 candidates: a high-quality 13B, a mid quantized 30B variant, and a small low-latency 7B that can be used as a fallback.
[00:56] Marcus Lee: can you show how you pick the quantized variants? our infra team is worried about kernel support and weird nv-ops.
[01:04] Priya Ramesh: sure — on the console, under "compatibility matrix" you can see kernel mappings per hardware type. note — sometimes the auto-detect lists 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' in autogenerated notes, so ignore that typo in older rows, but the mapping is accurate.
[01:20] Priya Ramesh: (screen share) here is the matrix — columns for model, quantization (8-bit, 4-bit), GPU kernels (cuBLAS/Triton), and cpu vector libs. we also surface sequence length limits and memory footprint estimates.
[01:35] Rosa Martinez: that memory estimate — is it including prefix/KV cache warmups? we plan to use long contexts ~8k tokens.
[01:42] Priya Ramesh: good question. estimates include a default KV cache allocation; for 8k you'll see a bump. i'll annotate the sheet to show memory delta at 4k/8k/16k contexts.
[01:53] Alex Chen: important tradeoff: quantized cpu runs can cut cost but sometimes increase p95. we usually recommend a split routing policy — primary to gpu-quantized model for quality, fallback to small low-latency model when under high load to keep tail latencies bounded.
[02:06] Marcus Lee: how do you measure quality differences? we need to avoid hallucinations on summarization.
[02:11] Priya Ramesh: our bench harness includes reference prompts and ROUGE/precision checks for summarization; we also do semantic similarity embeddings to detect meaning drift. we can run the zenith prompt set and surface per-model quality deltas.
[02:25] Alex Chen: i'll flag that we'll add a custom eval run for your prompts. send the 200 sample prompts to the email in the deck or via the shared drive link.
[02:34] Rosa Martinez: about networking — we require VPC peering and a narrow CIDR allow list. can you support private deployment with customer-managed KMS?
[02:42] Priya Ramesh: yes — Redwood Private supports bring-your-own-KMS (HSM integrations optional) and the control plane can be placed behind customer VPC. note: for on-prem air-gapped installs there's an extra ops playbook.
[02:54] Samir Khan: and SOC2 evidence? we need audit logs and retention settings.
[02:58] Alex Chen: we have SOC 2 Type II; i'll drop the compliance pack link. the console exposes audit logs and token-level usage export; retention is configurable at the enterprise tier.
[03:10] Marcus Lee: on routing — can you do region-aware routing? our users are EU and NA.
[03:15] Priya Ramesh: yes, routing policies can be per-route. you can set latency-first for EU or cost-first for background jobs. we also support model pinning per-route.
[03:24] Rosa Martinez: okay can you walk through a specific candidate — say the 13B high-quality model? what's the expected p95 on a single A100 equiv?
[03:31] Priya Ramesh: based on our verified runs, the 13B HF-ish model with kernel optimizations hits ~280-350ms p95 for a 1k-token request on an A100-class card, depending on prompt complexity and KV cache hit rate. if you enable continuous batching for throughput, p95 can change, so we recommend benchmarking with your distribution.
[03:51] Marcus Lee: that seems promising. cost-wise how do you model that? per-token + GPU-hour?
[03:56] Alex Chen: hosted is per-token plus model premium; Dedicated is committed capacity (monthly) with predictable GPU pool pricing. our pricing spreadsheet includes per-1M token estimates and example commits. i'll send a tailored sheet with examples using your expected qps.
[04:10] Samir Khan: concern: if we need private deployment, is the same catalog available? i.e., how do updates and rollouts work?
[04:16] Priya Ramesh: same catalog semantics — you can pin model versions and control rollouts. for Private we ship a private control plane that respects your release windows; rollouts can be canaryed across nodes.
[04:27] Rosa Martinez: earlier you mentioned fallback policies — can we do A/B tests for quality vs cost?
[04:31] Alex Chen: yes, the Console supports A/B experiments with automatic metrics collection. we can wire in your eval set to track regressions and set alerts.
[04:41] Marcus Lee: any gotchas with long contexts and quantization? we've seen quality drop at 8k context when using 4-bit quantized models.
[04:48] Priya Ramesh: true — quantization may affect attention scaling; we capture that in the compatibility matrix row called 'context stability'. for critical long-context tasks we often keep a denser FP16 variant or use hybrid routing (FP16 for long-context requests, quantized for short).
[05:02] Rosa Martinez: what's the expected timeline for a small POC? we need to show value to procurement by mid april.
[05:08] Alex Chen: proposed plan: this week you share prompts & target SLA; we run 3-candidate bench and deliver results in 5 business days. after you validate, we spin a 2-week POC (dedicated staging) starting early april. i'll include a milestone plan in the spreadsheet.
[05:22] Samir Khan: procurement will need contract terms and data residency info. can you provide an example SLA and DPA?
[05:29] Alex Chen: yes, i'll attach the standard SLA and DPA and the SOC2 report link.
[05:34] Marcus Lee: any competing vendors we should be worried about?
[05:37] Alex Chen: folks often evaluate with Anthropic/Vertex/OpenAI for hosted; for self-hosted runtimes there are infra vendors — we can share a competitive matrix.
[05:46] Rosa Martinez: last quick question — do you support prefix cache warmup across shards? we want warm cache in the tail for interactive chats.
[05:53] Priya Ramesh: yes, warmup and prefetch policies are configurable; we also support persistent KV cache for sessions. we'll note config options in the bench results doc.
[06:04] Alex Chen: ok, quick recap and next steps — alex to send pricing + bench template, priya to run dedicated staging tests after we get prompts, marcus/rosa to provide prompts and network constraints. we'll target the benchmark deliverable by 2026-03-29.
[06:18] Marcus Lee: sounds good, thanks both.
[06:20] Samir Khan: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[06:22] Rosa Martinez: thanks, bye.
